items.note: hamburg-business.com article (10 Aug 2020): plans presented in early August 2020 by the urban development and transport authorities and Hamburg-Mitte district office; from October only public transport (e.g. red city-tour buses), deliveries and bicycles permitted; called a temporary solution meant to pave the way for reconstruction from autumn 2021. The text correctly frames this as plans. Title matches.

PDF is the official Bürgerschaft Drucksache 21/20019 (written question by Thilo Kleibauer, CDU, 31.01.20, with the Senate's answer dated 07.02.20). It is hosted on the MP's own website, but the text is the official parliamentary document with the Senate's answer. The preliminary remarks say the annual card price was cut from 200 to 100 euros from 01.01.2019; that by the end of 2019 the P+R company had largely completed its takeover of the district P+R sites and introduced charges almost everywhere; and that occupancy sensing shows free spaces in real time on site and online. Title and date are fine.

The page says the Senate adopted the 'Strategie Mobilitätswende' on 28 November 2023, with a goal of 80% of trips by the Umweltverbund by 2030. The first of its ten fields of action is 'Mehr ÖPNV mit der Strategie Hamburg-Takt'. Title matches.

Press release dated 19 May 2026. It says fees have not changed since 2022. Zone 1 goes from 3.50 to 4.00 EUR; zones 2-4 each rise by 0.50 EUR. The resident permit rises from 65 to 70 EUR when applied for digitally (from 70 to 90 EUR in person). Meters switch over step by step in the coming weeks, and electric vehicles keep parking free up to the maximum time. It is presented as decided. Title matches.

The page is undated. It states electric cars may park free at all parking meters up to the maximum parking time, and that current law ends this privilege at the end of 31 December 2026. The text makes no claim beyond the page. The year-level date '2026' only reflects the expiry year and when the page was checked; no more specific date is supported. Title matches.

Press release of 18 June 2026: the pilot starts 7 July 2026 in two areas with ten neighbourhood parking zones (Harvestehude 4, Borgfelde/Hohenfelde/Uhlenhorst 6). At the meter or in the app, drivers enter their plate; parking tickets, resident and visitor permits no longer need to be displayed. A camera-equipped scan car checks plates against the parking-rights databases. The page <title> matches the draft (the on-page heading adds the kicker 'Abschaffung der Zettelwirtschaft'). The date is the pilot start, which is correct.

Press release of 8 July 2026: the scheme is extended to selected REWE and PENNY car parks (three pilot sites, 2 PENNY, 1 REWE), bookable digitally from 18:00 to 08:00 and all day on Sundays/holidays, at 3 EUR per night. The 'first city in Germany' claim is on the page. Two problems: the draft says 'residents' can book, but the page says the spaces are for residents and visitors; and it omits that this is a pilot ('Pilotprojekt').
items.corrected_text: The city extended its 'Feierabendparken' scheme in a pilot to three REWE and PENNY supermarket car parks, which residents and visitors can book digitally overnight and on Sundays for 3 euros per night. The city says Hamburg is the first city in Germany to include these chains.

items.note: The entwicklungsstadt.de article (14 April 2025) says Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier in HafenCity opened on 8 April 2025, with about 170 shops, food and leisure units, a multiplex cinema, three hotels, 579 homes and offices. Title matches.

The page shows 2,500 spaces, open 24 hours, dynamic pricing, a 39 EUR daily maximum, and a free first hour for Westfield Club members; all are confirmed. However, the page is undated (only a '© 2026' footer). 'As of October 2026' and the date 2026-10 reflect when it was accessed, not anything the page says, so they are reduced to the year.
items.corrected_text: Westfield's own undated parking page lists about 2,500 car spaces open 24 hours, dynamic pricing with a daily maximum of 39 euros, and a free first hour for members of its Westfield Club.

items.note: Designa reference page: go-live 2025, ticketless systems for short-term parkers plus FREEFLOW, 34 LPR cameras, dynamic pricing, mobile payment, and camera-based parking guidance with single-space detection. The draft title is only the page's category label. The HTML <title> tag is wrong (a template leftover reading 'Mid Valley Mega Mall'), and the on-page heading is 'WESTFIELD Hamburg-Überseequartier'.
items.corrected_title: Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier – A tailored parking solution for one of Europe's largest inner-city projects (Designa reference)

items.note: Press release 'Parkhaus wird Wohnhaus' dated 28 April 2025. The car park is at Neue Gröningerstraße 12, 20457 Hamburg (Altstadt, near St. Katharinen). It is to become 90 publicly subsidised cooperative units (Gröninger Hof eG). Preparatory work starts in May and demolition/refurbishment in summer. The draft correctly frames these as plans. The page title is fine (the full heading continues 'im Gröninger Hof können 90 öffentlich geförderte Wohnungen entstehen').

FashionUnited (1 Aug 2024): the operations of the three department stores (KaDeWe Berlin, Alsterhaus Hamburg, Oberpollinger Munich) were transferred to the new operating company KaDeWe GmbH and continue 'ohne Unterbrechung'. This followed the implementation of the purchase contract with the Thai Central Group signed in early June 2024. The former KaDeWe Group GmbH filed for insolvency in January amid the Signa crisis. Title matches.

electrive (11 Sept 2024): E.ON charging park with 18 points (5x50 kW, 4x150 kW stations) on the 7th deck of the car park at the newly opened MediaMarkt store (flagship) at Mönckebergstraße 1. It is publicly accessible during car park opening hours (7:30-22:00) and not only for MediaMarkt customers. Title matches.
electrive (14 Jan 2026): 'Der Schwerpunkt des Ausbaus lag 2025 auf Hamburg'. 55 charging points were activated at Hanseviertel, Gänsemarkt, Elbphilharmonie and Blankenese P1/P2. Title matches.

electrive (2 June 2026): 5,063 public charging points on 1 April 2026, which is 1,440 more than a year earlier (about 40%). It names a concession model used since 2025 as one basis for the growth ('unter anderem'), with five private operators building 500 points each. 'Helped by' matches this hedged wording. Title matches.

ZfK (20 Jan 2025). The figures are preliminary: the HVV 'rechnet mit' (expects) more than 1.1 billion journeys in 2024, which a transport authority spokesperson called a record, against 1.096 billion in 2019, the last pre-Covid year. The page does not call 2019 a record. Weekday ridership was about 2.7 million, up from about 2.55 million in the previous timetable year (+~6%). 'Recorded' overstates the certainty of preliminary figures.
items.corrected_text: According to preliminary figures cited by a transport authority spokesperson, the HVV expected more than 1.1 billion journeys in 2024, a record, compared with 1.096 billion in 2019. About 2.7 million passengers travelled on an average weekday, around 6 percent more than in the previous timetable year.

items.note: BWAI press release (18 Feb 2025). The 16.1 million overnight stays for 2024 (+1.1% on 2023) are 'nach aktuellen Hochrechnungen', i.e. a projection, not a final reported figure. The record 1.3 million cruise passengers and 77% hotel room occupancy are as stated. The page title is 'Hamburgs Tourismuswirtschaft hält weiter Kurs'; 'Neue Spitzenwerte' is only the on-page kicker above the heading and is not part of the page title.
items.corrected_text: The economics authority projected about 16.1 million overnight stays in 2024, 1.1 percent more than in 2023, and reported a record 1.3 million cruise passengers and hotel room occupancy of 77 percent.

corrected_summary: Hamburg presented plans in August 2020 to make the Jungfernstieg largely car-free from October 2020, and in November 2023 the Senate adopted a goal of 80 percent of trips by walking, cycling and public transport by 2030. In 2026 the city raised on-street parking fees for the first time since 2022 and began a pilot of licence-plate-based digital parking control. Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier opened in April 2025 with a ticketless, dynamically priced car park, a city-centre car park at Gröninger Hof is planned to become housing, and Hamburg counted 5,063 public charging points in April 2026, including new points in APCOA and MediaMarkt car parks.
